messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding a new customer on Private (VPC) who requires us to use their GCP KMS keys (customer-managed). Need quick agreement on the minimal service account model + rotation plan. They want audit logs in their project and an ability to rotate keys without downtime.

devon: +1. Short version: we should use a customer service account (SA) that we impersonate from our control plane, grant it only roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the cryptoKey, and keep the key ring in their project. That keeps key material in their boundary.

sanjay: Want to call out envelope encryption details here — runtime should generate ephemeral DEKs, encrypt payloads locally, then call KMS to encrypt the DEK (Encrypt API). Rewrap on rotation. No plaintext DEKs leave the instance memory except transient.

lina: Agree. For perms, customer can grant either the SA or a short-lived impersonation principal. Example minimal binding we use in onboarding: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/PROJECT/locations/global/keyRings/kr-name/cryptoKeys/key-name \
  --member="serviceAccount:REDCLOUD-PRIVATE-SA@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
```
Replace member with the customer's SA if they prefer self-managed identity.

maria: What about rewrap workflows? Customer expects zero-downtime rotation. We can't re-encrypt all stored blobs synchronously.

devon: We use lazy rewrap: create new cryptoKeyVersion, then mark it as primary. DEKs are rewrapped on first access (read path) or via background batch job. For large stores we offer a parallel rewrap worker that reads old ciphertext, decrypts locally using old key version, encrypts DEK with new key version, and writes back metadata. Important: maintain version history so rollback possible.

sanjay: Commands for rotation (create new version + set primary): 
```
# create new key version
gcloud kms keys versions create --key key-name --keyring kr-name --location global --project PROJECT
# optional: test encrypt/decrypt with new version id then set primary
gcloud kms keys versions set-primary --key key-name --keyring kr-name --location global --version 2 --project PROJECT
```
Note: set-primary is immediate; our rewrap path must be resilient to mixes of versions.

lina: Audit logging: customer must enable DATA_ACCESS audit logs for Cloud KMS in their project (so they see Encrypt/Decrypt/AsymmetricSign calls). We also emit our own request logs to the customer's audit sink if requested. Ask them to add log retention policy.

maria: Any concerns about IAM boundaries? The private deploy control plane runs in our management project; impersonation is via iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken with iamcredentials:generateAccessToken. We need iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the customer SA for that flow. Is that ok?

devon: We should prefer a short-lived impersonation grant (principals: our control-plane SA get iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the customer SA). Customer grants the actAs on their SA to our control-plane service account. That avoids giving our SA direct KMS perms. Example: 
```
# customer grants our control-plane SA permission to impersonate their SA
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding customer-sa@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member="serviceAccount:redwood-control@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
```
Then we impersonate and call KMS as the customer SA.

sanjay: Also consider organization policy constraints (e.g., restrictions on service account impersonation). Ask security to verify the customer's org policies during onboarding.

lina: Triage note: vuln question we saw — old library versions calling cryptoKeys asymmetric APIs leaking key version in logs. Remind engineers to scrub logs and never log ciphertext or key resource names beyond key-name and keyring.

maria: Good catch. Also: for incident response, if a key is compromised, we recommend: 1) disable or destroy key version, 2) create new key version and rotate, 3) start rewrap job with priority, 4) invalidate cached DEKs. Documented runbook: see deploy-bot link below.

deploy-bot: Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.example/kms-private-rotation (internal) :book: 

devon: Practical checklist for onboarding message to customer: 
- Do you want us to impersonate a customer SA or manage keys ourselves?
- Key ring & cryptoKey resource names + project id
- Desired rotation cadence (e.g., 90d) and whether they require immediate rewrap on rotation
- Audit log retention SLA
- Org-policy constraints / restricted SA impersonation

maria: I'll draft the onboarding email with the checklist and include the sample gcloud commands + a short diagram for envelope flow. Anything else?

sanjay: Add note about KMS quotas (Encrypt QPS) and how we fallback to cached DEKs when quota is hit. Also mention KMS regional restrictions if customer wants multi-region.

lina: +1. I'll add a blurb about least-privilege IAM and a small terraform snippet for customers who use infra-as-code.

maria: Great — thanks everyone. I'll send the draft to legal & compliance before sending to the customer. :thumbsup:
